Introduction to NGMS

Start here — concepts and architecture before anything else.

What is NGMS?

NGMS (Next Gen Media Server) is a unified media management server built in Rust. Series, movies, indexers, and download management are handled by a single application — one database, one configuration file, one web interface — with a shared library, shared download queue, and integrated indexer search.

It ships with embedded torrent and usenet download engines, so it can operate completely standalone: install it, point it at your media directories, add an indexer, and it will search, download, and organize your content automatically. External download clients (SABnzbd, qBittorrent, NZBGet) are also supported if you already run them.

✦
Built in Rust. A single process, minimal memory footprint, no JVM, no Python interpreter, no Node runtime. The binary starts in under a second.

Why unified?

Managing a media library typically means running separate applications for series, movies, and indexers — each with its own process, database, configuration, and web interface. Keeping them synchronized means duplicating quality profiles, wiring API keys between services, and coordinating upgrades across independent codebases.

NGMS is designed as a single application from the start. Every component shares one database, one configuration system, and one quality profile engine. There is nothing to keep in sync.

Core concepts

Eight concepts underpin everything NGMS does. Understanding these before touching any settings will save you a lot of confusion.

📺

Series

A TV show you want NGMS to track. When you add a series, NGMS fetches all episode metadata from TMDB, and then monitors for episodes you don't have yet. You control which seasons and episodes are monitored — only monitored items are automatically searched.

Found in: Series page

🎬

Movie

A film you want NGMS to track. Behaves similarly to Series but without episode structure. NGMS watches for the release date and will search automatically once the movie is available on your preferred sources.

Found in: Movies page

🔍

Indexer

A source NGMS queries to find releases — Newznab (usenet), Torznab (torrent), or a Cardigann YAML definition for custom sources. Indexers are configured once and shared across all searches for both series and movies.

Found in: Settings → Indexers

📦

Release

A specific file available for download, returned by an indexer search. A release has a name (e.g. Show.S01E01.1080p.BluRay.x265), size, categories, and a source URL or NZB file. NGMS evaluates each release against your quality profile before grabbing.

Used in: Queue, History

⭐

Quality Profile

A named set of rules — which resolutions are acceptable, in what priority order, and when to stop upgrading. For example: "accept 1080p or better; upgrade from 720p if 1080p appears; never upgrade once Bluray is grabbed." Every series and movie is assigned one profile.

Found in: Settings → Quality Profiles

⬇️

Download Client

Where files actually download to. NGMS supports embedded engines (built-in torrent via librtbit, built-in usenet via nzb-web) or external clients (SABnzbd, qBittorrent, NZBGet). You can configure multiple clients and assign categories or priorities.

Found in: Settings → Download Clients

📂

Import

The process of taking a completed download and moving (or hard-linking) it into your organized library. NGMS parses the filename, matches it to the correct series/movie/episode, applies your rename pattern, and places it in the right folder. Import can be automatic or manual.

Found in: Queue, Import page

🗂️

Library (Root Folder)

The root path where your organized media lives. You define separate root folders for series and movies, and NGMS places imported content there. Root folders must be accessible by the NGMS process — map Docker volumes accordingly.

Found in: Settings → Media Management

How it all fits together

Every automated grab follows this path:

🔍
Search Indexer queried (RSS or interactive)
↓
📋
Release Evaluation Parser extracts quality, language, episode info. Quality profile compared.
↓
⬇️
Grab Release sent to download client (embedded or external)
↓
✅
Download Complete Client signals completion; NGMS picks up the file
↓
📂
Import File renamed and moved to library root folder
↓
📡
Plex Scan Plex library section refreshed (if Plex integration enabled)

Embedded engines vs. external clients

NGMS ships with two built-in download engines. You don't have to configure anything external — NGMS can operate completely standalone.

Mode How it works Best for
Embedded torrent librtbit runs inside the NGMS process. Torrents are tracked internally, ratio rules apply, seeding is managed by NGMS. New installs, simpler setups, single-binary deployments.
Embedded usenet nzb-web runs inside the NGMS process. NZB files are downloaded, decoded (yEnc SIMD), PAR2 repaired, and extracted internally. New installs. Full pipeline in one process with no SABnzbd needed.
External (SABnzbd, qBittorrent, etc.) NGMS connects to the external client via its API. Downloads are managed by the external tool; NGMS only handles import when they complete. Existing setups, advanced per-client config, split hosts.
ℹ
Both embedded and external clients can be active simultaneously. NGMS routes grabs based on protocol (usenet/torrent) and client priority order.

Modules overview

NGMS is modular — each section of the application can be enabled or disabled independently via Settings → Modules. Navigation items hide themselves when a module is disabled.

ModuleWhat it does
SeriesTV show library — track, search, and organize episodes automatically
MoviesFilm library — monitor releases, quality upgrades, import
TorrentBuilt-in torrent client UI (librtbit engine)
UsenetBuilt-in usenet client UI (nzb-web engine)
SearchInteractive search across all configured indexers
DiscoverBrowse trending and popular content via TMDB
CalendarUpcoming episode and movie release schedule
StreamingDirect play and HLS transcode via ffmpeg
PlexPlex API integration — library scans, watchlist sync, activity view
RequestsMulti-user request and approval workflow
NotificationsDiscord, Telegram, Slack, email, webhook alerting
